views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the existing Section 301 tariffs in place and continue the Washington talks without new tariff hikes, rollbacks, or standalone purchase commitments. Press for a written, unilaterally enforceable deal on IP, forced tech transfer, and subsidies, using the still-suspended List 3 hike from 10% to 25% as unused leverage rather than a live trigger. Do not mix the Meng/Huawei criminal track into the trade text, and do not pre-commit to farm purchases until enforcement language is locked.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is a modest U.S. opportunity, not a crisis. After the 2018 tariff cascade (Lists 1–3 covering ~$250B, China matching on ~$50B plus ~$60B at 5–10%), Beijing is now bargaining: the Feb 24 delay of the List 3 hike, the Mar 28 reports of unprecedented Chinese offers on tech transfer, and the Apr 3 Washington round reporting progress on enforcement text all show U.S. leverage working. Markets and households are not signaling a trade-war emergency (VIX 13.74 on Apr 3; Michigan sentiment 97.2). That said, the opportunity is incomplete: Lighthizer still flags major hurdles, IP/subsidy practices remain the 301 core, and farm retaliation is biting (USDA: ~$7.9B soybean losses; ~27.5 million tons unsold; ~900 million bushels in storage). Industrial production has slipped (~1.7% over the window) and IMPCH is down ~26%, so costs are real but contained. Escalating now would likely stall a crunch-period text and deepen farm and input-cost pain; conceding purchases or rolling back tariffs before an enforceable structural deal would spend leverage for a May 2018-style purchase truce that already collapsed. Negotiate—hold the tariff stock, keep the unused 25% hike as a backstop, and only trade relief against written, snap-back enforcement.
key_factors: Crunch-period Washington talks (Apr 3) report progress on text/enforcement but no signed deal
U.S. tariff leverage intact: ~$250B still covered; List 3 10%→25% hike delayed twice and unused
China offering purchases and unprecedented tech-transfer language; structural IP/subsidy issues still open
Farm-belt retaliation is the main U.S. cost (soy unsold stocks, $12B aid) but not a macro crisis
U.S. risk assets calm (VIX ~14, sentiment recovered); IP soft and China imports down, so some real drag
Huawei/Meng + Canadian detentions are a parallel track that should not be bargained inside the 301 deal

sources_cited.excerpt: Intensive Washington talks between US and Chinese negotiators; both sides report progress on text, including enforcement language. No final deal signed.
Trump tweets that talks have made substantial progress and further delays the scheduled List 3 hike from 10% to 25%.
List 3 takes effect at 10%. China imposes retaliatory tariffs (5–10%) on ~$60B of US goods. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
G20 Buenos Aires dinner: 90-day negotiation window; planned Jan 1 List 3 hike suspended. Same day: Canada arrests Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou on a US extradition request.
VIX latest 13.74 on 2019-04-03; down from the Dec 2018 spike (36.07 on Dec 24), indicating low market stress at the decision date.
Michigan consumer sentiment 97.2 (2019-04-01), recovered from the January dip to 91.2.
U.S. goods imports from China 34,499 mil. $ (2019-04-01) vs 46,345 in Nov 2018, about -26% over the window.
U.S. industrial production 102.274 (2019-04-01), down ~1.7% from 104.068 in Nov 2018.
U.S. officials said progress in all areas, with unprecedented movement on forced technology transfers; IP and enforcement remained sticking points (Mar 28, 2019).

Lighthizer told Congress an enforcement mechanism was taking shape (monthly/quarterly/ministerial reviews, unilateral proportional action) but 'much still needs to be done' and Chinese practices still threaten the U.S. economy.
USDA chief economist: ~27.5 million tons of U.S. soybeans expected unsold in 2019; trade tensions cost soybean farmers $7.9 billion last year.
Record soybean stocks (~3.7B bushels in Dec); even pledged Chinese purchases would leave ~900 million bushels; $12B farm aid softened 2018 blow.
